regions.name: Tropical Evergreen Forests
features: Rainfall - Tropical evergreen vegetation is found in areas which receive over 200 centimetres of rainfall.
Temperature - The temperature ranges between 24°C and 27°C.
Location - Northeastern parts of India, the western slopes of the Western Ghats and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Important trees - Bamboo, rubber, mahogany, ebony and rosewood
Features of the trees - The trees in these forests do not shed all their leaves at the same time.
Fun Fact- The forests are home to the Malabar giant squirrel and the lion-tailed macaque.

regions.name: Thorn and Scrub Forests
features: Rainfall - Thorn and scrub forests are found in areas which receive less than 25 centimetres of annual rainfall.
Temperature –The temperature ranges from 25°C and 40°C.
Location- Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab and the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats.
Important trees – Thorny bushes, cactus, khair, babool and keekar
Features of the trees – The trees have long roots that go deep into the soil in order to absorb moisture. They also have long, fleshy stems and thick leaves to store water.
Fun Fact – These forests are home to blackbucks, desert foxes, and various reptiles like monitor lizards.

regions.name: Coniferous Forests
features: Rainfall – Connferous forests are found in areas which receive 150 cm to over 300 cm of annual rainfall.
Temperature – The temperature ranges from 11°C to 14°C.
Location – Mountain forests are found in the mountain areas of India, stretching from Kashmir to Assam. In the southern part of India, they are found in the hilly regions of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

Important trees – Sal and bamboo trees grow in the foothills of the Himalayas up to a height of 1,500 metres. Coniferous trees, such as pine, cedar and silver fir, are found between 2,000 and 3,300 metres. Juniper, pine, fir and rhododendrons are the main trees found in the alpine forests, which are above 3,300 metres.
Features of the trees– The trees have shallow but widespread root systems which help in anchoring them in rocky terrains.
Fun Fact- Rhododendron trees have beautiful flowers which are red, white and pink in colour and look stunning in full bloom.

regions.name: Deciduous or Monsoon Forests
features: Rainfall - Deciduous or monsoon forests are located in areas with 100 to 200 centimetres of rainfall.
Temperature – The temperature ranges from 20°C and 30°C.
Location – Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Karnataka
Important trees – Teak, sal, mango, shisham, neem and sandalwood
Features of the trees - These trees shed all their leaves during the dry season and grow new leaves during the spring season.
Fun Fact- These forests are home to Bengal tigers, Indian elephants, and sloth bears.

regions.name: Mangrove or Tidal Forests
features: Rainfall- Mangrove forests are found in areas which receive 100 cm to 300 cm of annual rainfall.
Temperature – The temperature ranges from 25°C to 35°C.
Location – The Sundarbans in West Bengal and in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Important trees - Sundari is an important tree species found in Sundarbans.
Features of the trees – Mangrove trees are highly salt tolerant and can grow well in brackish water.
Fun Fact- The Sundarbans in the Bay of Bengal is home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.
